rv.q: Running through Dec. 15, “Macbeth” is a solid, sometimes exceptional, production of one of Shakespeare’s greatest plays.
It’s an immersive and unforgettable experience that cements Invictus Theatre’s place among the top-tier Chicago theatre companies.

One of the more scrumptious bits of wickedness in Shakespeare’s most famous spook ’em is an offhand, unwittingly prophetic remark by Lady Macbeth, delivered to her waffling husband. “Things without all remedy should be without regard,” she reassures. “What’s done is done.”
Overall, this production of The Tragedy of Macbeth is passable.
This production of Macbeth is incredibly enjoyable.
In all, this is a good production that tells a tale about egomania, tyranny, and deviousness.

cn.t: Invictus Theatre's bold, atmospheric production earns mostly positive reviews for its raw intensity and supernatural elements, though some critics find it uneven. Strong performances and eerie design stand out in this potent take on Shakespeare's tragedy.
